newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Endesa outlines $1.5 bln deal with Enersis.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Endesa outlines $1.5 bln deal with Enersis.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa said on Friday its $1.5 billion deal to take a controlling stake in Chile's Enersis would significantly boost its presence in Latin American, but place no great burden on its finances.
In a statement given at a news conference following the announcement, Endesa said it had "taken a definitive step towards consolidating its international strategy."
"The amount of the operation is a maximum of $1.5 billion, which could be financed without a substantial modification in Endesa's debt levels," the firm added.
This converts the Endesa group into the controlling shareholder of the largest private electricity group in Latin America.
The move was well-received by analysts, who in principal see it boding well for the sale of a stake of up to 35 percent stake in Endesa by state holding company Sepi in the autumn.
"In principle, we think growth from Enersis for the next two years will be strong enough so that (the deal) is not dilutive (for Endesa)" said an analyst at a U.S. brokerage.

In a study using 1996 results as a model, Endesa said the deal would have boosted attributable profit by 19 percent in that year to 197 billion pesetas (versus 165 billion as reported), and would have increased gearing to 42.6 percent (versus 37.8 percent).

In a mandatory statement to the stock market watchdog CNMV, Endesa said earlier today the deal was worth an initial 193.0 billion pesetas ($1.24 billion) to acquire stakes in the Chispas group of investment firms, which control 29.04 percent of Enersis.
Enersis in turn controls Chile's largest power generator, also called Endesa.
The two utilities will set up a joint venture owned 55 percent by Endesa and 45 percent by the Chilean firm to invest in Latin America.

Enersis and Chispas' shareholders and employees who take up Endesa's offer to buy their shares will be offered the possibility of taking Endesa shares in exchange, up to a maximum of five percent of the Spanish firm's capital. These shares will be provided by Sepi, which controls 67 percent of Endesa.
Endesa shares trading on the bourse initially performed well, outstripping the Ibex-35 blue chip index, but later came down in line with the market.
The announcement comes hot on the heels of news Thursday that Endesa's rival Iberdrola is to lead a consortium which won a controlling stake in Brazilian power distributor Coelba for $1.6 billion.
A group including Endesa was also in the running for the Brazilian business.

"They have several plans on the boil in Latin America, and my impression is that as they didn't win in Brazil, they've speeded the Enersis deal up to have something positive to offer the market ahead of the public offering," a second analyst said.
